candidates.sec: Religious buildings near the Freedom Monument
candidates.name: Riga Orthodox Cathedral
candidates.content: The Orthodox Cathedral was erected during Russian rule for Russian residents. In contrast to its relatively plain exterior, it is spectacular on the inside, but be aware that shorts are not allowed.

candidates.sec: Religious buildings near the Freedom Monument
candidates.name: St. Gertrude Old Church
candidates.content: The brick neogothic church of St. Getrude, despite "old" in its name, is an entirely late 19th-century creation that replaced a series of stone and wooden churches that stood there (and were repeatedly destroyed due to being outsi

candidates.name: Latvian Academy of Sciences
candidates.content: Built in 1953, this building is often called "Stalin's Birthday Cake" because of its austere yet ornamented design. The 17th-floor balcony is open to visitors.

candidates.name: Triangula Bastion
candidates.content: A modern building with an excavated fragment of the historical fortification wall system along the river. The building has the best view terraces in Riga.

candidates.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: House of the Blackheads
candidates.content: The House of Blackheads is where the merchants-to-be had their guild. Part of this building is the tourist information office, the rest is a fascinating museum. The upper levels house grand ballrooms while the basement has a wine

candidates.name: Museum of the Occupation of Latvia
candidates.content: This noticeable and austere black building is clearly out-of-place. In the Soviet days, this housed a museum to the Red Riflemen, a group of Latvians who volunteered for the service to Russia during the Russian revolution of 1917.

candidates.name: Museum of Decorative Arts and Design
candidates.content: The Museum of Decorative and Design Art is located in the former St. George’s Church building (1204), which is the oldest stone building in Riga. It features seven collections of decorative and design art work.

candidates.name: National History Museum of Latvia
candidates.content: The History Museum is interesting, however there is little English (every room has its exhibits summarized on a single plaque). However, the museum does give a very good idea of Latvian history, and will give you a good understand

candidates.sec: Religious buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: St. Peter's Church
candidates.content: St. Peter's Church, dating to 1209, is Riga's oldest church. Besides its ensemble of architecture, the church has an elevator to the tower from where you can see all of Riga (service not available on Mondays).

candidates.name: Museum of the History of Riga and Navigation
candidates.content: Actually two museums plus a number of special exhibits, though you pay one price. English, German and Russian descriptions of each permanent collections are provided in a booklet inside each exhibit hall. Both of the main museums

candidates.sec: Museums near Powder Tower and City Wall
candidates.name: Latvian Museum of Pharmacy
candidates.content: In a renovated 18th-century house. The museum showcases pharmaceutical equipment, traditional medicine and herbs and what pharmacies looked like a century ago.

candidates.name: National Museum of Art
candidates.content: Latvian National Museum of Art is the most significant depository in the nation for works of art. Houses many works by Latvian artists.

candidates.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: The Large Guild
candidates.content: Housed the guild of the tradesmen, who would join after being a member of the Blackheads (see House of Blackheads). Home to the Latvian Philharmonic – you can't just walk inside. It's the exterior that's worth seeing though.

candidates.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: The Small Guild
candidates.content: Another pretty building just behind the Big Guild, this one housed the craftsmen's guild. Like the Big Guild, you can't go inside except for a performance.

candidates.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: The House of the Black Cat
candidates.content: This building (also housing a pub of no particular note) is most famous for the two statues of black cats on the roofs. The legend has it that a disgruntled tradesman who was not accepted into the Big Guild, built this house and p

candidates.name: Riga Film Museum
candidates.content: This museum holds various exhibitions that display different aspects of cinema art, actors and film history.

candidates.name: Porcelain Museum
candidates.content: Covers the history of porcelain in Riga through the 19th and 20th centuries.

candidates.name: Latvian National Museum of Art
candidates.content: Latvian National Museum of Art is the most significant depository in the nation for works of art.

candidates.sec: Religious buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: St. John's Church
candidates.content: A smaller, less spectacular church near Saint Peter's. There is a nice altar inside, and unlike most Riga churches, this one is free. The altar is from the Renaissance period and depicts the death, resurrection and ascension of Je

candidates.sec: Religious buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: St. Jacob's Catholic Church
candidates.content: Dating to 1226, this is one of the few Catholic churches left in Riga. At one point, it housed one of Riga's first schools.

candidates.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Cathedral Square
candidates.name: Riga Castle
candidates.content: One of the medieval castles in Latvia, on the bank of the river, which is now the seat of the Latvian president. The museum in the castle can be visited by the public.

candidates.name: Art Museum Riga Bourse
candidates.content: The Art Museum Riga Bourse stores the largest collection of foreign art in the Baltic states.

candidates.name: Riga Cathedral
candidates.content: Dating to 1207, the cathedral is one of Riga's symbols. The 6768-pipe organ inside is particularly spectacular. Besides the organ, however, the interior is rather Spartan, and may not be worth the entrance fee (even the organ is b

candidates.sec: Museums near Powder Tower and City Wall
candidates.name: Museum of War
candidates.content: 22 collections of Latvian and Soviet military equipment starting from World War I until today.

candidates.name: Russian Orthodox Church of the Annunciation
Jesus Church
candidates.content: An unusually-designed Lutheran church.

candidates.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: Statue of Roland
candidates.content: Statue of St. Roland, the patron of Riga. The original statue erected in 1897 was destroyed in World War II; now a replica stands there.

candidates.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Old Town Square
candidates.name: Town Hall
candidates.content: Pretty to look at, but not open for visitors.

candidates.name: Latvian National Opera
candidates.content: A pretty building in its own right, this is also a nice place to see an opera or ballet.

candidates.name: Playground
candidates.content: Youth sport festival that encourages and enables every visitor to try to explore inspiring sports and culture on water, land and air (e.g. longboarding, SUP, wakeboarding, hydro-cycles, mountain bikes, slack line).

candidates.name: Jāņi
candidates.content: On June 24, Latvians celebrate the summer solstice with the midsummer festival called Jāņi. Before the celebration, flea markets are held in many places.

candidates.name: Latvian Song and Dance Festival
candidates.alt: Latvian Vispārējie latviešu Dziesmu un Deju svētki
candidates.hours: Takes place once every 5 years, at the beginning of July
candidates.content: One of the key cultural events in Latvia, which started in 1873 as a singing festival. This festival has become an important facet of Latvian culture and has been held 25 times since then. There are smaller Song and Dance Festival

candidates.name: Riga Rhythms Festival
candidates.price: Some events cost €10-45, some are free
candidates.hours: Takes place annually, at the end of June/start of July; 18:00–00:00

candidates.name: Mikhail Chekhov Riga Russian Theater
candidates.hours: the booking-office is open daily from 12:00 till 19:00
candidates.content: Oldest Russian theatre in the world outside Russia.

candidates.name: Easter
candidates.content: Egg fights!

candidates.name: Count of May
candidates.content: Medieval festival. Takes place annually in mid-May.

candidates.name: Latviabeerfest
candidates.content: Takes place annually at the end of May. The largest international beer festival in the Baltics.

candidates.name: Rīga City Day
candidates.hours: Takes place the whole of August
candidates.content: Traditional weekend of celebrating a city. Many cultural events take place all around the city.

candidates.name: White Night
candidates.hours: Annually, in the beginning of September

candidates.name: Arena Riga
candidates.content: An indoor sports arena and concert venue. Notable as the home rink of the city's ice hockey team Dinamo Riga, playing in the KHL, the arena is also where the world's greatest pop and rock artists and bands hold their Riga concerts

candidates.name: Theater-Club "Hamlets"
candidates.content: Riga Theater-Club in heart of old city.

candidates.name: Koncertzāle Ave Sol
candidates.content: Hosts the renowned choral ensemble Ave Sol. The hall also plays host to a range of other concert activities.

candidates.name: Lattelecom Marathon
candidates.hours: Held in the middle of May
candidates.content: The biggest sport marathon held since 2007 in Latvia.

candidates.name: Riga Zoo
candidates.content: The Riga Zoo is small, but fairly popular.

candidates.name: Backpackers Pub
candidates.content: Riga’s first Aussie pub promises to provide plenty of authentic down under atmosphere, but thankfully without any stuffed koalas, Fosters beer posters or, God forbid, any portraits of Paul Hogan. Spread out across three floors, th

candidates.name: Pūce
candidates.price: Entrance: free + face control. Beer: €2-3, Long drinks: €4-6, Cocktails: €6-9
candidates.content: A trendy place popular with a younger crowd. The main floor has a dance floor with rock and pop music while the basement has a room with techno and/or alternative sounds. It is a very busy place on Th F Sa and is closed on Su M.

candidates.name: French Bar
candidates.content: One of the cheapest, smallest, and oldest bars in Riga. It is popular among foreigners and local students. TV shows international sports matches.

candidates.name: Skyline Bar
candidates.content: Just perfect view at sunset. Finding a table next to the windows might be difficult after 23:00. Cover charge at popular times.

candidates.name: Neo Bars
candidates.content: Enjoy the view of Riga from the 10th floor of the Central Station clock tower. Drinks, cocktails, European and Japanese cuisine. You need to take the elevator from the Central Station ground floor to the 8th to 10th floor.

candidates.name: Alus Bārs
candidates.content: A very local bar, literally "the beer bar". Like going back in time to the turbulent 1990s. Open Monday to Saturday from 12:00 to anytime in the evening from 19:00 to 23:00.A can of Cēsu €2.2050 cl of Mītava €2.5050 cl of Piebalga

candidates.name: FolkKlubs Ala Pagrabs
candidates.content: Huge beer selection with 28 beers on tap, folk dancing, live music performances, and great authentic food.

candidates.name: Funny Fox Bar
candidates.content: A karaoke and sports bar. Great place to duck in and have a few jars. A very wide selection of songs and drinks, with a great atmosphere and stuff on the TVs. The karaoke is really fun and it's an intimate setting.

candidates.name: Black Magic
candidates.content: A very cool place with a decor that will remind you of Harry Potter or Lord of the Rings. Very atmospheric. Perhaps the best place to try different types of black balsam, with flights and tastings here, lots of flavors to choose f

candidates.name: Kalku Varti
candidates.content: Ground-level restaurant with nightclub in the basement.

candidates.name: Leningrad
candidates.content: Serves Latvian beers and food.

candidates.name: Godvil
candidates.content: Nightclub.

candidates.name: Cuba Cafe
candidates.content: Cozy bar with DJs in the evenings. Salsa dancing on Tuesdays starting at 21:00. 2-for-1 drinks during happy hour (17:00-19:00).

candidates.name: Lido Entertainment Center
candidates.price: Cafeteria: €3.30 for a meat main course and €0.70 for a plateload of roast potatoes. Pancakes for €0.60. Top floor: Buffet for set price of €16
candidates.hours: Main restaurant: daily 11:00-23:00, express restaurant: daily 13:00-23:00, beer cellar: Mon-Fri 18:00-00:00, holidays 12:00-00:00, playroom: Mon-Fri 17:00-22:00, holidays 12:00-22:00
candidates.content: The wooden building features three floors of dining, a built-in wooden windmill, and a small amusement park outside. The ground floor and basement operate cafeteria-style. There is a huge choice available, including a variety of s

candidates.name: Alus Arsenals
candidates.content: A nice, cozy restaurant in the Riga old town serving various meat and fish oriented dishes with quality local beer. Located right next to the Riga castle so it's easy to find. The actual interior of the restaurant is in a cellar,

candidates.name: Čili Pica
candidates.content: Cheap but good pizza.

candidates.name: Vermanitis
candidates.price: Fried fish €3, salmon steak €5, half chicken €2.50, large side of mashed potatoes or pasta €1, 500 ml beer €2.10
candidates.content: A fantastic range of Latvian food in "authentic" environment.

candidates.name: Vincents
candidates.content: If you're splashing out try Vincents Restaurant which compares favorably to any up market western restaurant at half the price.

candidates.name: Šašliki Mangaļos
candidates.content: Popular with locals. They offer shashlik on a skewer with a choice of chicken, lamb or beef, with tomato sauce and a side of vegetables or Armenian flatbread. Beverage options include various local beers, Georgian wine or softdrin

candidates.name: Lido
candidates.content: A network of 8 restaurants offering decent hearty Latvian food, including desserts, at good prices. The restaurants are either cafeteria-style or feature English menus.

candidates.name: Stargorod
candidates.content: Traditional Czech and Latvian cousine, brewery, beer, tours in brewery, entertainment

candidates.name: Fontaine Delisnack
candidates.content: Fast food, open 24/7.

candidates.name: Ezītis miglā (Avotu iela)
candidates.content: Reasonably priced drinks and food, nice atmosphere.

candidates.name: Riga Central Market
candidates.hours: Different hours for different parts, see website for info
candidates.content: Noticeable for its huge hangars, built from parts of actual Zeppelin hangars bought for the market in 1920. The market has also a large open-air area. It deals mostly in fresh food and is a good place for fresh local fruit and veg

candidates.name: Bergs Bazaar
candidates.content: The Bergs bazaar is a 19th-century courtyard passage with a number of fashion boutiques, restaurants and a farmers' and crafts market on the second and fourth Saturday of each month.

candidates.name: Āgenskalns Market
candidates.content: This is a smaller counterpart to the Central Market, to be found the central square of Āgenskalns on the left bank of Daugava, which is a crossing of no less than 6 streets. An impressive building from 1911-23, remarkable as a red

During the Christmas season there is a small Christmas market in the main square of old town which offers lots of festive fare and hot wine.

december.sec: Monuments and historic buildings near Old Town Square
december.text: Riga monument to Christmas tree: First Christmas tree in Riga was in 1510!
